Core Algorithm

Building a Physics-Based Lot Pressure Engine

How we use fluid dynamics principles to model parking lot occupancy as a pressure system. Real-time updates from geofence triggers feed our machine learning models, predicting availability with 94% accuracy across all Rutgers lots.

Read the deep dive →
📊
Data Science

The 'Vulture' Metric: Correcting Arrival Sampling Bias

Our proprietary Vulture Metric corrects for the temporal bias in parking arrival data. Most apps only see users actively searching; we've built a background daemon that detects true occupancy changes, eliminating the "ghost lot" problem.

Questions & Answers

Everything You Need to Know

No. We use smart geofences that activate data collection only when you're near campus. Background activity is minimal—we're talking single-digit percentage impact. Most users report no noticeable battery drain.

No, ScarletSpots is built by students for students. We're independent, but we're better. We lack the bureaucracy of official apps and move faster based on direct user feedback. We're also completely free.

Our physics-based forecasting model achieves 94% accuracy across all Rutgers lots. We combine real-time geofence data with historical patterns and machine learning to predict where you'll find a spot. Like weather, perfect prediction isn't possible, but we're remarkably close.

Your anonymized location data and parking session info train our models to make predictions better. We never sell your data. We're open-source at heart and transparent about how we use information. Check our privacy policy for full details.

You can browse live occupancy data without logging in. To unlock friend finder, personalized predictions, and parking history, you'll need a quick sign-up with your university email. Takes 30 seconds.

ScarletSpots is live now on the iOS App Store for Rutgers students. Android version is in beta. We're rapidly expanding to other universities—join the waitlist to be notified when we arrive at your school.
